localKernel.gateTitle: Signed in — connecting to the desktop app
localKernel.deviceSlotHint: Signing in to the website does not use a device slot. This device is registered only after the browser connects to the desktop app. Registered devices can be removed in device management.
localKernel.gateSubtitle: The web app automatically connects to MedHelp Desktop running on this computer. After its window is closed, the desktop app can remain online in the system tray.
localKernel.browserRecoveryHint: Open MedHelp Desktop first. If it is already running in the system tray, allow Local Network Access for app.medtimehelp.com, then retry.

localNetworkPermission.title: Allow this page to connect to the App engine
localNetworkPermission.description: The desktop App can provide its Local Engine to this browser; this is not an account restriction. Chrome and Edge separately ask whether this site may access services on this computer.
localNetworkPermission.instructions: Open the site information control on the left of the address bar, set Local Network Access to Allow, then refresh or select “Retry after allowing”. This only connects to 127.0.0.1 on this computer and does not expose the engine to the internet.

appDownload.title: Download the MedHelp Desktop App
appDownload.description: The Local Engine is built into the desktop app. Install it and keep it running so website sign-in can connect automatically.

benefits.builtIn: The Local Engine is included—no terminal commands to copy
benefits.simple: Automatic launch, connection, updates, and tray background mode
benefits.secure: Research files and execution remain on this computer

appDownload.windowsInstallBody: Run the downloaded EXE. If Microsoft Defender SmartScreen appears, first confirm that the file came from this site, then choose More info → Run anyway.
appDownload.macInstallBody: Open the DMG and drag MedHelp into Applications. If macOS says the developer cannot be verified, try opening the app once, then go to System Settings → Privacy & Security → Security and choose Open Anyway.
appDownload.macDamagedHint: If macOS reports that the app is damaged, open Terminal and run:
